## How they got there
Inter reached the final as runners-up after losing to Paris Saint-Germain 0-5. Their path was defined by a dominant profile, sitting in the top tier for points per game at 2.38 where they were better than 94% of that season's group-phase teams, while also limiting opponents with just 2.9 shots on target per game to rank higher than 89% of their peers. This efficiency extended to a goal difference per game of 1.25, placing them ahead of 88% of the league phase competition.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Inter for this run, as they ranked 7th by probability and fell outside its top two choices. Although their chance to reach the final was calculated at 12.9%, which exceeds the base rate of 8.3% for a random knockout team, the system's expectation aligns closer with the quarter-finals rather than the summit. This discrepancy highlights that while Inter outperformed the average probability, they were not among the highest-ranked teams in the model's historical training data.

## Weak spots
The analysis identifies three clear areas where the team lagged behind most of their contemporaries. They covered only 68.1 km per game, a figure better than just 3% of that season's group-phase teams and 0% since 2011-12, while also recording a shot accuracy of 39.2% that surpassed only 8% of their peers in the same phase. Additionally, they generated 38.4 attacks per game, which was better than only 35% of the group-phase teams and 46% of all Champions League teams since 2011-12.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
